prompt:
A traditional East Asian ink-wash painting (sumi-e) on one plain sheet of warm, light rice paper with fine fibres, seen flat from straight above, evenly lit, no shadow, no frame, no table, no text, no letters, no numbers, no signature, no red seal, no stamp. Paint it the way a master ink painter works: a few confident, loose brush strokes, wet ink bleeding softly into the paper, dry-brush texture where the brush runs out, simplified forms that suggest rather than describe, lots of white paper. It must look like a painting, expressive and artistic, with the brushwork of the reference picture: never a realistic drawing, never a detailed illustration, never a pencil sketch, never a 3D render. Copy only the reference's brushwork, never its subject: no bird, no crane, no reeds, no water, no landscape. Only the things named below are painted: no mountains, no pine trees, no hills, no ground, no soil, no extra plants or objects. Sumi ink only, from deep black to soft grey washes, plus real gold leaf only where stated. Generous empty paper on every side. The subject fills most of the picture (about 85% of its height and width): bold, generous, never small in the middle of empty paper.

A small, shallow, round porcelain dish, seen from slightly above, painted in a few pale grey strokes with a darker rim, filling the middle of the picture. In the dish lie three or four small pieces of raw green propolis: sticky plant resin that glows like amber, painted in clear, luminous washes of olive-green-gold ink with real gold leaf glinting along their edges and bright highlights where the light passes through them; precious and clean, like small pieces of amber or jade, never like dirt, soil, rock or ore. Beside the dish on the right, lying on the same level, one vegetarian capsule, a few confident pale grey strokes with a fine darker outline and a small soft shadow, no gold on it. Nothing else. Simple, quiet, precious.
